items.title: Preprint claims the matrix multiplication exponent is 9/4
items.what_happened: A preprint in OpenAI's math repository, dated 24 November, claims the exponent of square matrix multiplication is 9/4 over every field.
items.why_it_matters: Matrix multiplication sits under most of machine learning. A result like this would settle a long-studied bound.
items.what_to_watch: Independent checks by complexity theorists and any published formal verification.
items.uncertainty: A new claim. I have not seen independent review. It says nothing about practical speed.

items.title: Two labs report proofs that VP and VNP are different
items.what_happened: OpenAI posted a preprint claiming VP is not equal to VNP. Posts say Anthropic published its own proof hours earlier.
items.why_it_matters: This is the algebraic cousin of P versus NP, open for decades. It would be a landmark for AI-assisted maths.
items.what_to_watch: Expert review of both proofs and whether they use the same idea.
items.uncertainty: Claims are fresh and I have not seen independent review.

items.title: Preprint claims the polynomial Hirsch conjecture is false
items.what_happened: A preprint in OpenAI's math repository claims superpolynomial graph diameter for simple polytopes, which would disprove the conjecture.
items.why_it_matters: The question bears on how fast the simplex method for linear programming could ever be.
items.what_to_watch: Whether optimisation researchers confirm the construction.
items.uncertainty: Not independently reviewed as far as the source shows.

items.title: METR updates its AI task time horizon plot
items.what_happened: METR reports some capabilities are still rising exponentially, while models are weaker at judgment tasks than at coding.
items.why_it_matters: The plot is widely cited in forecasting and policy, so its limits matter.
items.what_to_watch: The full report's task mix and how judgment tasks are scored.

items.title: AISI: attack policy choice can mislead monitor evaluations
items.what_happened: The UK AI Security Institute published a case study on how choosing the attack policy can undermine claims that a monitor is reliable.
items.why_it_matters: AI control and monitoring results may look stronger than they are.
items.what_to_watch: Whether monitor papers start reporting how attack policies were chosen.

items.title: Eugene Yan on where 12 public evals break
items.what_happened: Eugene Yan wrote up how benchmarks are built, the bugs they have and what should change.
items.why_it_matters: A practical checklist before trusting or building a benchmark.

items.title: MIT: physics constraints keep chaotic-system models stable
items.what_happened: MIT researchers report that enforcing physics-based constraints stops AI models from making unreliable predictions for complex nonlinear systems.
items.why_it_matters: Relevant to weather, climate and turbulence models and to scientific machine learning.
items.what_to_watch: Tests on longer rollouts and real data.

items.title: Solomonoff induction with reflective oracles
items.what_happened: A paper shared on the Alignment Forum studies a version of Solomonoff induction built with reflective oracles.
items.why_it_matters: It suggests self-reflection can help a predictor cope with sources outside its hypothesis class.

items.title: CMU essay on provable safety for capable agents
items.what_happened: A CMU ML Blog post discusses guarantees that keep capable agents open to human correction, such as honouring a stop request.
items.why_it_matters: It frames corrigibility as a property to prove, not only to test.
items.what_to_watch: Whether the guarantees hold under realistic assumptions.

items.title: Agents write small programs into an LLM's weights
items.what_happened: A researcher reports using Claude to write small modules that bolt onto model weights to patch failure modes, shown on Qwen3-0.6B.
items.why_it_matters: A possible route to editable, inspectable fixes without retraining.
items.what_to_watch: Results on larger models and independent reproduction.
items.uncertainty: Self-reported, on a very small model.

items.title: OpenAI describes defences against adversarial distillation
items.what_happened: OpenAI outlined layered defences: model training, safeguards, detection and enforcement against capability extraction.
items.why_it_matters: Shows how labs are treating model outputs as something to protect.
items.what_to_watch: Effects on ordinary research use of APIs.

items.title: MedChemBench tests models on early drug discovery
items.what_happened: OpenAI introduced a benchmark on reading molecular structures, reasoning from experiments and choosing compounds.
items.why_it_matters: A more applied test of scientific reasoning than quiz questions.
items.uncertainty: Built and reported by a model developer.

items.title: NVIDIA on speeding up RL rollouts
items.what_happened: NVIDIA published guidance on reducing inference bottlenecks in reinforcement learning rollouts with Dynamo.
items.why_it_matters: Rollout speed often limits how much RL training is affordable.
items.what_to_watch: Reported gains outside NVIDIA's own setup.

items.title: Multilingual AI points to a shared neural code for meaning
items.what_happened: An MIT study of speakers of 21 languages finds the brain may represent meaning in much the same way across them.
items.why_it_matters: A neat link between language models and neuroscience.
items.what_to_watch: Replication with more languages and other imaging methods.

items.title: Anthropic interviews 58 companies on AI and work
items.what_happened: Interviewed firms described few layoffs but reduced hiring, and said the most valuable uses often came from reorganising roles.
items.why_it_matters: Qualitative evidence on how deployment changes work.
items.what_to_watch: Whether labour data shows the same hiring pattern.
items.uncertainty: A vendor study of its own customers.
